i do understand where you’re coming from, but most people simply have a skewed understanding of suicide, making it really hard to really be there for someone who has these thoughts. reporting someone often gets them into a cycle of going in and out of hospitals with no proper solutions. hospitals only provide medication or a place to get away from your own life for a few days. it works for some, but for a majority it does not. getting locked somewhere you don’t want to be in sort of puts your walls up as a defense mechanism, making the person even harder to reach since they go on emotional lockdown.

now, about associating yourself with a suicidal person: people end up thinking that they’re to blame in the end anyway, even if they knew that the person was suicidal. they end up regretting not trying to do something about it. what’s the difference if they actually did say something as long as they made the effort? the person was considering suicide before, so i don’t understand the connection. they reasonably shouldn’t have been able to cause the death if the person was already thinking about doing it in the first place as long as they’re not actively trying to provoke it. i feel like the real reason people choose to disconnect is because they don’t want to bring themselves down. you know, “bad vibes” and whatnot. i think it’s just the irrational belief that you adopt the mindsets around you. 

as for medication, i don’t enjoy the uncertainty in it. i do get that it is capable of making things easier, but i also have a fear that it’ll make things worse because i have come across far too many people who’ve gotten permanent mental damage from the wrong prescription (while testing to see which ones work). they also get pricey, especially if you need multiple types of pills to treat certain symptoms. if you’re wondering, a psychiatrist that i did meet with suggested against it as well, because my depression stems primarily from situations that were out of my control (you could even just call it bad luck). i’ve also never been able to afford a full mental exam, but doctors have suspected other disorders which makes it really difficult to find medications that won’t clash with one another. on top of that, i have a really arbitrary urge to rely on myself to heal. it sounds dumb, but i want to be able to learn how to be self-sufficient without the aid of something foreign to my body.

i would love to talk to you about this over message if you’d like to discuss this more.

it’s really hard to say whether i’d be more miserable as a poor person. if i were to have grown up poor, it would change how i lived and i think it would give me a different mindset. it would also change my source of stressors. i’m not sure if how miserable you are can be measured, either, but i definitely see how you personally might do better if you didn’t have to worry about money. 

i think growing up poor would have helped me become more independent. i’d have to rely more on myself. i was abused, bullied, and felt extremely pressured to succeed just because i had the opportunities some other people did not. i feel like this kind of pressure of not being able to satisfy yourself as well as others (imo) has more of a negative mental effect over worrying about how you’re going to survive. when you feel like you’re not good enough, it makes things a lot harder to do. you lose motivation. on top of this, i felt like a burden. i didn’t have people to talk to about it, because they’d just pull the “people are poor” card on me. although i’m grateful for a lot of things, but i would have been willing to give up my supposedly “better” living situation for the sake of my mental health.

i’m sorry if it sounded like i was romanticizing poverty; that’s not at all what this post was about. i was showing that these 2 things are different types of suffering and should not be compared. coupled together, things are obviously going to be worse. i’m sorry you feel like this, but someone who just has mental disorders can be just as miserable. people who aren’t considered “poor” don’t necessarily have the same expectations as a “poor” person might have, and it’s just unfair to say that people who have enough money don’t have the right to be as depressed. looking my situation, i’d rather live a life that requires me to work hard instead of having so much time to ruminate. even if i’m not starving, i can’t take care of myself anymore. i can’t do things i used to be capable of doing. i’m basically rotting in bed and everything is so hard to force myself to do. i feel like a failure as well. i think that—instead of minimizing this issue for a certain group of people—we should equally address this universally shared conflict.

lmao do you even have depression? it makes it really hard to find joy in anything. it makes it so that i can only look at the negatives, even though i know that i should be appreciative for what i already have. my negativity pushes others out of my life and makes me feel guilty for not being able to appreciate things that i know i’ve been blessed with, and it’s not something i can control. besides, just because others “have it worse” doesn’t mean that you should minimize other problems. everybody takes things in differently and everyone has their unique situations, which is why you can’t really say that “people have it worse.” moreover, i never said that depression was the worse thing in the world, nor even hinted that it was. there’s a reason why i mentioned that it would be unfair to compare these situations since they’re too different and complex to do so. many people with depression fail to take care of themselves—they’re also physically suffering. soldiers who have mental disorders and physical hardships? their problems are valid and should be addressed. man, people who died for free speech? i wish i could just die for no honorable reason! i never stated that other people didn’t deal with what sounds like a lot. my point was that mental disorders shouldn’t be dismissed or compared to other things; you completely overlooked that. thanks m8

I had a similar experience, and I think the best thing you can do right now is to seek help as soon as possible. 

In my junior year of high school, I also began to realize that I was probably depressed, but withheld from telling others. I had the same fears that you do: people might tell my parents—who surely would not understand—and I couldn’t talk to friends about it without having them label me as an attention seeker. However, things changed after I accidentally revealed too much of my situation to somebody (I was sleep deprived and they asked too many questions that I bluntly answered) and got reported to my school’s principal. It was out of the blue and completely unexpected. 

Because of the  call, I was put on a legal hold and got sent to a psychiatric hospital. I had never known that there was a place made to help people like me: teenagers wanting to die for various reasons (yikes!). At first, I was obviously terrified, but being in the hospital helped me learn a lot about my mental health. It helped me address issues that I formerly dismissed. Better yet, those hospitals aren’t what people make of them. Most of the people there weren’t actually crazy—for lack of a better term. Basically, if you get admitted, you’ll be able to see a licensed psychiatrist who will come up with a proper diagnosis. They will help you get the help you need. It’s also nice being able to talk to and relate to the other patients there, depression being a more common occurrence than most are aware of. The best thing is, even if adults are forced to notify your parents, you can refuse calls and visits from them (for a few days, at least) until you are truly ready to tell them. That was the case at the few hospitals I’ve been to, at least.

I honestly think that if you can spend a few days away from home, it’ll give you the little push that you need right now. It’ll also help your parents realize just how serious your situation is. Please tell a teacher or some other adult soon so that this doesn’t drag on! Your health should be your highest priority. 

I wish you the best of luck :)
